m1-append-override-entry.title: Add _append_override_entry; re-point _append_trip_entry onto it
m1-append-override-entry.imperative: Add a top-level `_append_override_entry(cl, kind, **fields) -> str` using the same setdefault('override_ledger', [])/append-only idiom as _append_trip_entry, ids scoped ov-N across all kinds. Re-point _append_trip_entry to call it with kind='trip' plus the existing trip fields (gate, verb, outcome, fill, hard, model, why_ref); _trip_hard_gate remains the only caller of _append_trip_entry, unchanged. Do not touch begin_over_line_records* yet (next item). Run `python -m pytest tests/test_checklist_engine.py -k trip -q` and confirm it is still fully green (regression floor, unmodified tests).

postconditions.statement: _append_override_entry exists; _append_trip_entry re-pointed to it; all existing -k trip tests still pass unmodified

constraints: never mutate/remove an existing ledger entry
flat entry dict: id/kind/ts plus **fields, no nesting

status_detail.blocker: Handoff requires (5) checklist_engine.py never writes trip_ledger again after this gate, AND (Close Criteria/Protected Intent) every existing -k trip test in tests/test_checklist_engine.py passes UNMODIFIED. These two requirements conflict: ~34 of ~123 -k trip tests directly index cl['trip_ledger'][0]/assert its raw content after driving a FRESH trip through dispatch() (e.g. test_ledger_entry_carries_every_field_including_the_live_why_ref at :6807, test_hard_refusal_leaves_state_unmutated at :3862 via the _without_trip_ledger helper at :3753 which only pops 'trip_ledger' not 'override_ledger'). With writes re-pointed to override_ledger per spec, trip_ledger stays empty for anything written post-migration, so these assertions fail -- not from any behavioral regression (sampled several: dispatch/refusal/immutability semantics are byte-identical), purely from the storage relocation the gate itself mandates. Fixing this needs either (a) editing ~34 pinned test assertions plus the _without_trip_ledger helper to read through _override_entries/override_ledger instead of raw trip_ledger, which Allowed Scope permits touching the test file for but Close Criteria's own 'passes UNMODIFIED' and 'do not delete or weaken existing trip-ledger assertions' argue against without explicit sign-off, or (b) dual-writing trip_ledger, which requirement 5 explicitly forbids. Not resolving unilaterally per Authority ('stop and report why rather than silently choosing a different shape') and Stop Conditions ('an existing trip-ledger test cannot be made to pass unmodified... [if only] changing trip storage' is named as the exact non-blocking case, but 34 tests is not an edge case, it's the bulk of the suite baked into pinned raw-key assertions).
status_detail.next_action: Confirm whether Allowed Scope's test-file pre-authorization covers rewriting these ~34 raw-trip_ledger-key assertions (and the _without_trip_ledger helper) to read through _override_entries/override_ledger instead -- this is what 'unmodified' cannot mean literally once storage moves, or clarify a different intended reading.

m2-override-entries-read-path.title: Add _override_entries; rewire begin_over_line_records(_historical) to read through it
m2-override-entries-read-path.imperative: Add `_override_entries(cl, kind=None) -> list[dict]`: yields cl.get('trip_ledger', []) entries first, each retagged kind='trip' in the returned dict only (never written back), then cl.get('override_ledger', []) entries; filter by kind when given. Rewrite begin_over_line_records (:2192) and begin_over_line_records_historical (:2230) to source from _override_entries(cl, kind='trip') instead of cl.get('trip_ledger') directly -- read-path swap only, outcome/why_ref filtering logic unchanged. Run `python -m pytest tests/test_checklist_engine.py -k trip -q` again to confirm the swap changed nothing observable.

postconditions.statement: _override_entries exists with legacy-first merge order and kind filter; begin_over_line_records(_historical) read through it; -k trip tests still pass unmodified

constraints: trip_ledger is read here only, never written/migrated in place
legacy-first order is fixed, not sorted by timestamp

m3-new-tests.title: Add the three required new tests
m3-new-tests.imperative: In tests/test_checklist_engine.py add: (1) a fixture using ONLY override_ledger (no trip_ledger key) with kind='trip' entries, asserting begin_over_line_records/_historical behave identically to a trip_ledger-only fixture; (2) a fixture carrying BOTH legacy trip_ledger and an override_ledger with an unrelated hand-constructed kind (e.g. force-claim), asserting _override_entries(cl, kind='trip') shows no leakage and no dropped legacy entries; (3) a live-transition fixture with legacy tl-1/tl-2, then drive a real start/reopen refusal through _trip_hard_gate so _append_trip_entry/_append_override_entry actually run, asserting _override_entries(cl) with no kind filter returns tl-1, tl-2, ov-1 in that order. Run the full test file.

postconditions.statement: three new tests added and passing; full test_checklist_engine.py green

constraints: do not delete or weaken existing trip-ledger assertions
